1	"""Pydantic models for all persisted records, plus the canonical JSON writer.
2	
3	Every artifact on disk is produced through :func:`canonical_dumps` so that two
4	builds with the same seed and provider are byte-for-byte identical.
5	
6	Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — the post lists what a
7	    shard actually holds: "Bloom Filters: used to quickly check if phrases exist",
8	    "Each shard has a trained Zstandard text compression dictionary", and
9	    "Vocabulary: the set of unique words in this shard" (shard 11,343 is quoted at a
10	    vocabulary of 64,992 terms). :class:`ShardManifest` had none of those three, so
11	    they are added here as first-class manifest fields. Local copy:
12	    ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``
13	
14	Assumptions: the post does not say how the three artifacts are serialised, so the
15	    two binary ones travel base64 inside JSON — the bloom bit array as the payload
16	    produced by :meth:`cybernaut_mini.shard_artifacts.PhraseBloom.to_payload`, the
17	    zstd dictionary as a bare base64 string. All three fields default to ``None``
18	    because a shard too small to train a dictionary on is legitimate (the tail of a
19	    k-means split) and because a manifest held in memory usually does *not* carry
20	    them: :class:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex` deliberately leaves them
21	    unpopulated and fetches them per shard on demand, since 1,000 resident
22	    vocabularies of 65,536 terms is gigabytes of heap.
23	
24	Alternatives rejected: a single ``artifacts`` sub-model holding all three. Rejected
25	    because the three have genuinely different lifetimes — the bloom is ~1.2 KB and
26	    cheap to keep, the vocabulary is the one that cannot be held 1,000 times over —
27	    and one field would force an all-or-nothing load. Also rejected: validating
28	    ``artifact_version`` inside the models. A model that refuses to parse an old
29	    record cannot produce the error message that tells the user which version they
30	    have; that check belongs at the index boundary, in
31	    :meth:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex.load`.
32	"""
33	
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import json
37	import math
38	from datetime import datetime
39	from typing import Any
40	
41	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator
42	
43	#: Bumped to "2" when shards gained their bloom filter, zstd dictionary and
44	#: vocabulary, and the index layout gained per-shard artifact sidecars and
45	#: JSONL offset sidecars. A "1" index has none of those files, so it is rejected
46	#: at load rather than read as a shard set with three permanently-absent
47	#: artifacts — see :meth:`cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex.load`.
48	ARTIFACT_VERSION = "2"
49	
50	FLOAT_DECIMALS = 8
51	
52	
53	def _round_floats(value: Any) -> Any:
54	    if isinstance(value, float):
55	        if not math.isfinite(value):
56	            msg = f"non-finite float in artifact: {value!r}"
57	            raise ValueError(msg)
58	        rounded = round(value, FLOAT_DECIMALS)
59	        return 0.0 if rounded == 0 else rounded
60	    if isinstance(value, dict):
61	        return {key: _round_floats(item) for key, item in value.items()}
62	    if isinstance(value, list):
63	        return [_round_floats(item) for item in value]
64	    return value
65	
66	
67	def canonical_dumps(obj: Any) -> str:
68	    """Serialize to deterministic JSON: sorted keys, compact, floats at 8 decimals."""
69	    return json.dumps(_round_floats(obj), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
70	
71	
72	def model_canonical_dumps(model: BaseModel) -> str:
73	    return canonical_dumps(model.model_dump(mode="json"))
74

76	class Document(BaseModel):
77	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
78	
79	    id: str = Field(min_length=1)
80	    title: str
81	    text: str
82	    url: str | None = None
83	    language: str | None = None
84	    published_at: datetime | None = None
85	    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
86	
87	    @field_validator("title", "text")
88	    @classmethod

90	        if not value.strip():
91	            msg = "must be non-empty"
92	            raise ValueError(msg)
93	        return value

96	class MetadataFilter(BaseModel):
97	    """Typed metadata filter; fields combine with logical AND.
98	
99	    ``extra="forbid"`` makes any unsupported operator a validation error.
100	    """
101	
102	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
103	
104	    language: list[str] | None = None
105	    published_from: datetime | None = None
106	    published_to: datetime | None = None
107	    metadata_equals: dict[str, Any] | None = None
108	
109	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
110	        return (
111	            self.language is None
112	            and self.published_from is None
113	            and self.published_to is None
114	            and self.metadata_equals is None
115	        )
116	
117	    def matches(self, document: Document) -> bool:
118	        if self.language is not None and document.language not in self.language:
119	            return False
120	        if self.published_from is not None and (
121	            document.published_at is None or document.published_at < self.published_from
122	        ):
123	            return False
124	        if self.published_to is not None and (
125	            document.published_at is None or document.published_at >= self.published_to
126	        ):
127	            return False
128	        if self.metadata_equals is not None:
129	            for key, expected in self.metadata_equals.items():
130	                if document.metadata.get(key) != expected:
131	                    return False
132	        return True

166	    #: is base64 inside it). ``None`` means "not loaded / not built", never "empty":
167	    #: an empty shard still gets a real, always-false filter.
168	    phrase_bloom: dict[str, Any] | None = None
169	    #: Base64 of this shard's trained Zstandard dictionary. ``None`` when zstd
170	    #: refused to train — a shard of a handful of short documents does not contain
171	    #: enough repeated material — in which case
172	    #: :func:`cybernaut_mini.shard_artifacts.compression_score` scores it 0.0.

176	    #: largest field a manifest can carry, which is why it is loaded per shard on
177	    #: demand rather than with the manifest.
178	    vocabulary: dict[str, Any] | None = None

183	        This is the form the manifest takes on disk and in memory: the payloads live
184	        in a per-shard sidecar so that loading 1,000 manifests stays cheap.
185	        """
186	        return self.model_copy(
187	            update={"phrase_bloom": None, "zstd_dictionary": None, "vocabulary": None}
188	        )

190	    def has_artifacts(self) -> bool:
191	        """True when all three artifact fields are populated on this instance."""
192	        return self.phrase_bloom is not None and self.vocabulary is not None

2	
3	All JSON-bearing datasets serialize through :func:`cybernaut_mini.models.canonical_dumps`
4	so pipeline outputs keep the byte-for-byte determinism guarantee.
5	
6	Every path the corpus and the index travel goes through a dataset in this module,
7	so the catalog — not a node body — owns all file and network I/O. That is what makes
8	``kedro-viz`` show real lineage and what lets ``conf/prod`` swap a local corpus for a
9	Hugging Face one without touching pipeline code.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import os
15	from pathlib import Path
16	from typing import Any
17	
18	import numpy as np
19	import numpy.typing as npt
20	from kedro.io import AbstractDataset
21	from kedro.io.core import DatasetError
22	
23	from cybernaut_mini.models import canonical_dumps
24	
25	#: Committed fixture directories. A pipeline writing here would silently rewrite the
26	#: golden corpus that the determinism tests compare against, so saves are refused.
27	#: Reads are unaffected — `--input data/sample/documents.jsonl` stays supported.
28	PROTECTED_DIRS = ("data/sample", "data/00_reference")
29	
30	
31	def _guard_protected(filepath: Path) -> None:
32	    """Refuse to write over a committed fixture."""
33	    try:
34	        relative = filepath.resolve().relative_to(Path.cwd().resolve())
35	    except ValueError:
36	        # Outside the project (e.g. a pytest tmp_path); nothing to protect.
37	        return
38	    as_posix = relative.as_posix()
39	    for protected in PROTECTED_DIRS:
40	        if as_posix == protected or as_posix.startswith(f"{protected}/"):
41	            msg = (
42	                f"refusing to write {as_posix}: {protected} holds committed fixtures. "
43	                f"Point this catalog entry at a generated layer "
44	                f"(data/01_raw, data/02_intermediate, data/03_primary) instead."
45	            )
46	            raise DatasetError(msg)

1	"""Normalisation of an external corpus into validated :class:`Document` records.
2	
3	The acquisition pipeline pulls rows in whatever shape the source publishes them
4	(the NOSIBLE Hugging Face datasets use ``text`` / ``label`` / ``netloc`` / ``url``)
5	and this module maps them onto the project's own schema. The field mapping is data,
6	not code, so a second source — the NOSIBLE Search API, a local dump — only needs a
7	new ``field_map`` in ``conf/``, never a new normaliser.
8	
9	Determinism
10	-----------
11	Document ids are derived by hashing the source's natural key, so re-running the
12	pipeline over the same pinned revision yields the same ids, and therefore the same
13	shard assignments and the same byte-for-byte index.
14	
15	Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — the "Documents" node
16	    that opens the build-time half of the architecture diagram, upstream of text
17	    processing and embedding. Local copy:
18	    ``data/00_reference/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.
19	
20	Assumptions:
21	    - A public corpus contains junk. Rows that are empty or shorter than
22	      ``min_text_chars`` are skipped, not raised on, because one malformed row out
23	      of 100,000 must not fail a multi-hour production build.
24	    - The source's ``url`` is a natural key. Where it is absent the body text is
25	      hashed instead, so every row still gets a stable id rather than colliding on
26	      the empty string.
27	    - Passages arrive untitled. A title is derived from the first sentence because
28	      the shard manifest, the shard summary, and the ``title\\ntext`` embedding
29	      input all assume one exists.
30	
31	Alternatives considered:
32	    - A normaliser class per source: the obvious object-oriented shape, and the
33	      right one once sources need genuinely different logic. Rejected while the
34	      difference between sources is only *which column holds what*, which a
35	      declarative ``field_map`` expresses without new code.
36	    - Sequential ids (``doc-000001``): shorter and readable. Rejected because they
37	      depend on row order, so re-fetching a corpus whose rows were reordered would
38	      renumber every document and silently invalidate the stored judgments.
39	    - Raising on unusable rows: better for a small curated corpus where every row is
40	      supposed to be valid. Rejected here for the reason in the assumptions above.
41	"""
42	
43	from __future__ import annotations
44	
45	import hashlib
46	import re
47	from typing import Any
48	
49	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
50	
51	from cybernaut_mini.models import Document
52	
53	#: Cap on a derived title. Long enough to be a useful routing signal, short enough
54	#: that it does not swamp the body text when the two are concatenated for embedding.
55	_TITLE_MAX_CHARS = 120
56	
57	_SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")
58	_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
59	
60	
61	class CorpusSourceConfig(BaseModel):
62	    """How to turn raw source rows into :class:`Document` records."""
63	
64	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
65	
66	    #: Source column -> Document field. Values must name real Document fields.
67	    field_map: dict[str, str] = Field(
68	        default_factory=lambda: {
69	            "text": "text",
70	            "url": "url",
71	        }
72	    )
73	    #: Source columns copied verbatim into ``Document.metadata``.
74	    metadata_fields: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
75	    #: Applied when the source carries no per-row language column.
76	    default_language: str | None = "en"
77	    #: Prefix for generated ids, so documents from different sources cannot collide.
78	    id_prefix: str = "doc"
79	    #: Drop documents whose body is shorter than this (boilerplate, nav text).
80	    min_text_chars: int = Field(default=32, ge=0)
81	
82	
83	class CorpusNormalizeError(ValueError):
84	    """Raised when a source cannot be mapped onto the Document schema at all."""
85	
86	
87	def _clean(value: Any) -> str:
88	    """Collapse whitespace in a source value; non-strings become empty."""
89	    if not isinstance(value, str):
90	        return ""
91	    return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", value).strip()
92	
93	
94	def derive_title(text: str) -> str:
95	    """Use the first sentence as the title, truncated on a word boundary.
96	
97	    These corpora ship passages without titles, but the shard manifest, the shard
98	    summary, and the ``title\\ntext`` embedding input all assume one exists.
99	    """
100	    first = _SENTENCE_END.split(text, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
101	    if not first:
102	        first = text.strip()
103	    if len(first) <= _TITLE_MAX_CHARS:
104	        return first
105	    clipped = first[:_TITLE_MAX_CHARS].rsplit(" ", 1)[0].strip()
106	    # A single token longer than the cap leaves nothing after rsplit; hard-cut it.
107	    return clipped or first[:_TITLE_MAX_CHARS]
108	
109	
110	def make_document_id(prefix: str, natural_key: str) -> str:
111	    """Stable id from the row's natural key, so ids survive a re-run."""
112	    digest = hashlib.blake2b(natural_key.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=8).hexdigest()
113	    return f"{prefix}-{digest}"
114	
115	
116	def normalize_rows(
117	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
118	    config: CorpusSourceConfig,
119	) -> list[Document]:
120	    """Map raw source rows onto validated, deduplicated :class:`Document` records.
121	
122	    Rows that are unusable — no body text, or shorter than ``min_text_chars`` — are
123	    skipped rather than raised on: a 100k-row public corpus is expected to contain
124	    some junk, and one bad row must not fail a production build. Duplicate natural
125	    keys collapse to their first occurrence. Ordering is by document id so the
126	    result is independent of the source's row order.
127	
128	    Raises :class:`CorpusNormalizeError` only for problems that make the *whole*
129	    source unusable, such as a ``field_map`` that never resolves a text column.
130	    """
131	    if not rows:
132	        return []
133	
134	    text_sources = [src for src, dest in config.field_map.items() if dest == "text"]
135	    if not text_sources:
136	        msg = "field_map must map exactly one source column onto 'text'"
137	        raise CorpusNormalizeError(msg)
138	    text_source = text_sources[0]
139	
140	    available = set(rows[0].keys())
141	    if text_source not in available:
142	        msg = (
143	            f"source column {text_source!r} (mapped to 'text') is absent from the "
144	            f"corpus; available columns: {sorted(available)}"
145	        )
146	        raise CorpusNormalizeError(msg)
147	
148	    documents: dict[str, Document] = {}
149	    for row in rows:
150	        text = _clean(row.get(text_source))
151	        if len(text) < config.min_text_chars:
152	            continue
153	
154	        fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
155	        for source_field, dest_field in config.field_map.items():
156	            if dest_field == "text":
157	                continue
158	            value = _clean(row.get(source_field))
159	            if value:
160	                fields[dest_field] = value
161	
162	        metadata = {
163	            name: row[name] for name in config.metadata_fields if row.get(name) is not None
164	        }
165	
166	        # Prefer the source url as the natural key; fall back to the body so rows
167	        # without one still get a stable id rather than colliding on the empty string.
168	        natural_key = fields.get("url") or text
169	        doc_id = make_document_id(config.id_prefix, str(natural_key))
170	        if doc_id in documents:
171	            continue
172	
173	        documents[doc_id] = Document(
174	            id=doc_id,
175	            title=fields.get("title") or derive_title(text),
176	            text=text,
177	            url=fields.get("url"),
178	            language=fields.get("language") or config.default_language,
179	            published_at=fields.get("published_at"),
180	            metadata=metadata,
181	        )
182	
183	    return [documents[key] for key in sorted(documents)]

82	    metadata_equals: dict[str, Any] | None = selection_params.get("metadata_equals")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL qrels → Judgment loader                                      #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

_MIRACL_ID_PREFIX = "mir"


def load_miracl_judgments(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[Judgment]:
    """Map structured MIRACL en-dev rows onto :class:`~cybernaut_mini.models.Judgment` records.

    The catalog entry for ``miracl_en_dev_source`` is backed by
    ``HuggingFaceDataset("miracl/miracl", config="en", split="dev")``, which returns
    rows with four fields: ``query_id`` (str), ``query`` (str), ``positive_passages``
    (list of ``{docid, title, text}`` with relevance grade=1), and
    ``negative_passages`` (list of ``{docid, title, text}`` with relevance grade=0).

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — the evaluation
        substrate used to record per-mode recall/nDCG/MRR baselines. Local copy:
        ``data/00_reference/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

    Assumptions:
        - ``relevant_document_ids`` holds ALL graded docids (both 0 and 1), not only
          the positives. The Judgment model stores ``dict[str, int]`` so both grades
          survive; downstream eval nodes compute nDCG correctly from the full set.
        - Docids are keyed as ``make_document_id("mir", passage["docid"])`` to match
          the ``id_prefix="mir"`` used by the MIRACL corpus ingest branch. A judgment
          whose docids use bare MIRACL strings would never match any Document.id.
        - A query row with zero assessments (empty positive AND negative lists) is
          silently skipped rather than raised on; MIRACL en-dev has none of these, but
          robustness beats a fragile length check.

    Alternatives rejected:
        - Accepting raw TSV bytes (``{query_id}\\t{question}`` + TREC qrel format) as
          two separate function arguments. Rejected because the structured
          ``miracl/miracl`` Hub dataset gives the same information already parsed, so
          separate TSV parsing adds code without adding insight.
        - Including only grade=1 docids. Rejected because nDCG requires the full
          relevance pool to distinguish true negatives (grade=0 but retrieved) from
          un-judged documents.

    Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``rows`` is empty (a configuration error — an
    empty MIRACL source is never valid).
    """
    if not rows:
        msg = "MIRACL source returned zero rows; cannot build judgments from an empty dataset"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    judgments: list[Judgment] = []
    for row in rows:
        query_id = str(row["query_id"])
        question = str(row.get("query", ""))

        relevant: dict[str, int] = {}
        for passage in row.get("positive_passages", []):
            doc_id = make_document_id(_MIRACL_ID_PREFIX, str(passage["docid"]))
            relevant[doc_id] = 1
        for passage in row.get("negative_passages", []):
            doc_id = make_document_id(_MIRACL_ID_PREFIX, str(passage["docid"]))
            relevant[doc_id] = 0

        if not relevant:
            # A query with no assessed passages contributes nothing to evaluation.
            continue

        judgments.append(
            Judgment(
                query_id=query_id,
                question=question,
                relevant_document_ids=relevant,
            )
        )

    return judgments


def validate_judgments_against_corpus(
    judgments: list[Judgment],
    corpus_doc_ids: set[str],
) -> None:
    """Assert every judgment docid exists in the built corpus.

    Raises :class:`ValueError` listing up to 20 missing docids so the operator
    can diagnose which MIRACL passages were dropped by the corpus filter step.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — acceptance
        criterion: "Every docid in miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl exists in the
        built index." A judgment over a missing doc silently caps recall.

    Assumptions: the corpus ids are passed as a ``set`` so the ``in`` check is O(1)
        per docid rather than O(n). Building the set once before calling this is the
        caller's responsibility.

    Alternatives rejected: returning the list of missing ids and leaving it to the
        caller to decide whether to raise. Rejected because a missing docid is never
        acceptable — it would silently cap recall — so failing loudly is the only
        correct behaviour.
    """
    missing: list[str] = []
    for judgment in judgments:
        for doc_id in judgment.relevant_document_ids:
            if doc_id not in corpus_doc_ids:
                missing.append(doc_id)

    if missing:
        sample = sorted(missing)[:20]
        msg = (
            f"validate_judgments: {len(missing)} judgment docid(s) absent from corpus "
            f"(first 20): {sample}. "

class MiraclTsvDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
    """Read MIRACL topics + qrels from Hugging Face Hub TSV files.

    ``load_dataset("miracl/miracl", ...)`` is blocked by a deprecated loading
    script (``miracl.py``). This dataset reads the underlying TSV files directly
    via :class:`huggingface_hub.HfFileSystem` and reassembles them into the same
    structured row format that ``load_dataset`` would have returned::

        {
            "query_id": str,
            "query": str,
            "positive_passages": [{"docid": str}, ...],   # grade 1
            "negative_passages": [{"docid": str}, ...],   # grade 0
        }

    This shape is exactly what :func:`cybernaut_mini.corpus.load_miracl_judgments`
    expects, so no downstream code changes are needed.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — MIRACL as the
        qrels source for eval; docid stability requires using the same TSV files
        that define the qrel identifiers, not a post-hoc HF conversion.
        Local copy: ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

    Assumptions:
        - Topics TSV format: ``{query_id}\\t{question}`` (no header, UTF-8).
        - Qrels TSV format: ``{query_id}\\tQ0\\t{docid}\\t{grade}`` (TREC-style,
          no header). Only grades 0 and 1 appear in MIRACL en-dev.
        - Topics with no matching qrel rows are silently dropped (they carry no
          judgment signal and ``load_miracl_judgments`` would skip them anyway).

    Alternatives rejected:
        - Fixing the ``miracl/miracl`` loading script upstream: out of scope for
          this educational replica.
        - Parsing the dataset via ``HuggingFaceDataset`` with a custom config:
          ``datasets`` refuses to load *any* dataset with a deprecated script.
        - Fetching the topics + qrels as two separate Kedro datasets and merging
          in a node: doubles the catalog boilerplate and adds a merge node just
          to satisfy HF's file layout. Wrapping both files in one dataset class
          keeps the Kedro graph identical to the ``load_dataset`` design.

    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``).
    """

    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo_id: str,
        revision: str,
        language: str,
        split: str = "dev",
        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
    ) -> None:
        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}."
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        self._repo_id = repo_id
        self._revision = revision
        self._language = language
        self._split = split
        self._token_env = token_env

    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        try:
            from huggingface_hub import HfFileSystem
        except ImportError as exc:
            msg = (
                "MiraclTsvDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        token = os.environ.get(self._token_env) or None
        fs = HfFileSystem(token=token)

        lang = self._language
        split = self._split
        rev = self._revision
        base = f"datasets/{self._repo_id}@{rev}/miracl-v1.0-{lang}"
        topics_path = f"{base}/topics/topics.miracl-v1.0-{lang}-{split}.tsv"
        qrels_path = f"{base}/qrels/qrels.miracl-v1.0-{lang}-{split}.tsv"

        # --- topics: query_id → question ---
        topics: dict[str, str] = {}
        try:
            with fs.open(topics_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    line = line.rstrip("\n")
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    parts = line.split("\t", 1)
                    if len(parts) == 2:
                        topics[parts[0]] = parts[1]
        except DatasetError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({self._repo_id!r}): failed to read topics "
                f"from {topics_path!r}: {exc}"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        # --- qrels: query_id → (positives, negatives) ---
        positives: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
        negatives: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
        try:
            with fs.open(qrels_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    line = line.rstrip("\n")
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    parts = line.split("\t")
                    if len(parts) < 4:
                        continue
                    qid, _q0, docid, grade_str = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
                    entry = {"docid": docid}
                    if grade_str.strip() == "1":
                        positives.setdefault(qid, []).append(entry)
                    else:
                        negatives.setdefault(qid, []).append(entry)
        except DatasetError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({self._repo_id!r}): failed to read qrels "
                f"from {qrels_path!r}: {exc}"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        # --- assemble rows (only topics that have qrel rows) ---
        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for qid, question in topics.items():
            pos = positives.get(qid, [])
            neg = negatives.get(qid, [])
            if not pos and not neg:
                continue
            rows.append(
                {
                    "query_id": qid,
                    "query": question,
                    "positive_passages": pos,
                    "negative_passages": neg,
                }
            )
        return rows

    def save(self, data: None) -> None:
        msg = (
            f"MiraclTsvDataset({self._repo_id!r}) is read-only; write the "
            f"normalised judgments to a JsonlDataset in data/02_intermediate instead."
        )
        raise DatasetError(msg)

    def _exists(self) -> bool:
        return False

    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "repo_id": self._repo_id,
            "revision": self._revision,
            "language": self._language,
            "split": self._split,
        }
